categoryName: Hair care — shampoo, conditioner, hair oil, colour, serum, styling

skuLines.line: Everyday family shampoo — large value bottle
skuLines.examples: Clinic Plus Strong & Long, Sunsilk Black Shine, Chik, Nyle Naturals
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; slight dip in deep winter (fewer washes)
skuLines.notes: Thin-margin traffic driver — the price the whole store is judged on. Long uncut hair means ml-per-wash is roughly double a plains household, so the large pack is the real family unit here, not the 180ml.

skuLines.examples: Clinic Plus, Sunsilk, Dove Daily Shine, Pantene
skuLines.notes: The hostel-room pack. Fits a locker, survives a shared bathroom, and is what a student buys when the 1L is out of pocket-money reach.

skuLines.examples: Clinic Plus 5ml, Chik, Sunsilk, Nyle, Head & Shoulders sachet
skuLines.packSizes: 5-8ml sachets, sold loose or as 16/30-piece strips
skuLines.notes: Lowest margin in the category and non-negotiable anyway — it is the entry price point for 5-18 year olds on pocket money. Hang the strip at the counter; loose-sachet pilferage is the one real shrink risk. Tiny cube, so freight per rupee of sale is poor — order deep and rarely.

skuLines.examples: Head & Shoulders, Clinic All Clear, Dove Dandruff Rescue, Himalaya Anti-Dandruff
skuLines.seasonality: STRONG winter spike (Nov-Feb) — dandruff is documented to worsen in cold weather; also a post-monsoon bump
skuLines.notes: The single most seasonally predictable line in this category at a cold hill site. Dry cold scalp plus a turban or patka worn all day plus infrequent winter washing is a dandruff engine. Build 2-3x depth for Nov-Feb; a February stockout here sends wallets to town.

skuLines.examples: Head & Shoulders sachet, Clinic All Clear sachet
skuLines.notes: Lets a student treat a flare-up without committing ₹200. Pair on the same hanger as the plain shampoo strip.

skuLines.examples: Dove Hairfall Rescue, Indulekha Bringha, Himalaya Anti-Hair Fall, Tresemme Hair Fall Defence
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon spike (Jul-Sep) — seasonal shedding complaints peak in the Indian monsoon
skuLines.notes: Heavy monsoon at this site makes hairfall the loudest complaint of the year. Culturally amplified: for people keeping uncut hair, shedding is not a cosmetic worry but a religious one, so willingness to pay is far above the national average.

skuLines.examples: Patanjali Kesh Kanti, Himalaya Protein, Dabur Vatika, Khadi Natural, Biotique
skuLines.notes: A Kalgidhar Trust township skews decisively natural/Ayurvedic. Better margin than the HUL/P&G mass lines and less price-compared, so this is where the category actually earns. Patanjali in particular travels well on trust, not advertising.

skuLines.line: Traditional wash — reetha / shikakai / amla powder or liquid
skuLines.examples: Khadi Reetha Shikakai, Patanjali, Banjara's, loose local reetha-shikakai-amla mix
skuLines.notes: Not nostalgia — soapberry/shikakai/amla washing is the documented pre-shampoo Indian practice and remains live among older women and observant households washing very long hair. Loose powder is high-margin. Powder cakes in a heavy monsoon: keep it off the floor and in sealed jars.

skuLines.examples: Mamaearth, WOW Skin Science, Minimalist, Plum, Arata
skuLines.notes: The Eternal University 18-25 cohort knows these brands from Instagram and will otherwise order them on a town trip or a home visit. Best margin in the shampoo shelf. Keep narrow — 3-4 SKUs, not a wall.

skuLines.examples: Johnson's Baby, Himalaya Baby, Mamaearth Gentle Cleansing, Sebamed Baby
skuLines.notes: Married staff quarters with infants have no substitute and no alternative shop. A baby-shampoo stockout is the classic reason a young family makes a 30-50km round trip and then buys a month of everything else in town.

skuLines.line: Kids shampoo / 2-in-1 detangling for school children
skuLines.examples: Mamaearth Kids, Johnson's Kids Shiny Drops, Chicco
skuLines.notes: Genuinely functional for 5-12 year olds with long tied hair who are combed by a warden or parent — detangling reduces the daily crying and the breakage.

skuLines.examples: Mediker Anti-Lice, Licel, Nix, Permite lotion
skuLines.seasonality: Outbreak-driven; predictably 2-4 weeks after each term start when children return to shared dorms
skuLines.notes: THE highest-regret SKU in this whole category for this specific site. 5-18 year olds in residential dorms, head-to-head contact is the dominant transmission route, ages 4-14 are the peak-infestation band and girls are infested 2-4x more than boys. An outbreak needs treating for a whole dormitory in the same week, so stock in DEPTH, not one facing. Always sell with a steel nit comb. Note permethrin-based lotions sit closer to the drug counter than the cosmetic shelf.

skuLines.examples: Nizral 2% (ketoconazole), Scalpe Plus, Danclear, Selsun
skuLines.notes: LICENCE CONSTRAINT — ketoconazole 2% and selenium sulfide are drug-schedule products in India, not cosmetics. These belong on a pharmacy/drug-licence counter, not the POS beauty shelf. Cosmetic zinc-pyrithione shampoo needs no such licence and covers most of the demand; refer the resistant cases to the campus health room rather than stocking these without the licence.

skuLines.examples: WOW Apple Cider Vinegar, L'Oreal Anti-Hard Water, Pilgrim
skuLines.notes: Worth a trial facing only if the township's spring/borewell water is genuinely hard or mineral-heavy — check that before buying, because the claim only sells where residents already complain about limp, coated hair.

skuLines.examples: BBLUNT Back to Life, Bombay Shaving Company, Batiste
skuLines.seasonality: Winter — when washing long hair in a cold hill bathroom is genuinely unpleasant
skuLines.notes: Small but real: drying waist-length hair at 5°C with no geyser time is the problem this solves. Aerosol — flammable, store away from heat, and confirm your transporter accepts aerosols on the hill route.

skuLines.examples: Clinic Plus 5L / 1L refill pouch, Himalaya institutional pack, local bulk fill
skuLines.notes: Not a walk-in SKU — a standing indent to the Academy's junior hostels and wardens who bathe the youngest children. Low margin but zero impulse risk, predictable, and it moves volume through the warehouse rather than the POS.

skuLines.examples: Sunsilk, Dove Intense Repair, Tresemme Keratin Smooth, Clinic Plus
skuLines.notes: At most Indian stores conditioner is optional; here it is not. Hair that is never cut, combed twice daily with a kangha and tied into a joora will snap without conditioning — so this is a functional purchase, not a premium one. Expect an unusually high conditioner-to-shampoo attach rate and buy accordingly.

skuLines.examples: Sunsilk, Dove, Tresemme sachet
skuLines.notes: Hang alongside the shampoo strip so the pair is bought together.

skuLines.examples: Tresemme Hair Mask, L'Oreal Total Repair 5, Mamaearth, Indulekha, Godrej Professional
skuLines.notes: Long dry winter hair plus a weekly hostel ritual makes this move better here than the ₹208 average bill would suggest. Buys as a treat, not a staple — a 2-3 SKU shelf is enough.

skuLines.examples: Livon Hair Serum, Streax Leave-in, Mamaearth Detangling Spray, Wella
skuLines.notes: Under-appreciated fit. Twice-daily combing of uncut hair is exactly the use case a detangler exists for, and it is what a warden or mother reaches for on a squirming 7-year-old. Push it as 'combing without tears', not as a beauty product.

skuLines.line: Hair serum — frizz control and shine
skuLines.examples: Livon Serum, Streax Vitalized, Bombay Shaving Company, Parachute Advansed serum
skuLines.notes: Livon-type silicone serum is the mass-market bridge SKU between oil and premium care and moves reliably in small towns. Stock the 20ml trial size — it converts at a ₹208 bill.

skuLines.line: Scalp / hair-growth serum with named actives
skuLines.examples: Minimalist Redensyl 3%, Mamaearth Rosemary, WOW Onion, Foxtale, Deconstruct
skuLines.notes: The fastest-growing premium sub-segment nationally and the top of the price ladder you can credibly hold here. Keep to 2-3 SKUs. Do NOT extend this into minoxidil — 2%/5% topical minoxidil is a prescription drug-schedule product in India and needs a drug licence, so it is a health-room referral, not a POS line.

skuLines.examples: Mamaearth Onion, WOW Onion, Indulekha Bringha, Wishcare
skuLines.notes: Onion has gone fully mainstream and now sells on shelf recognition alone. Sells best as an oil+shampoo pair — merchandise them together rather than in their own category blocks.

skuLines.examples: Parachute, Nihar Naturals, Shalimar, Cocoraj
skuLines.notes: Almost certainly the single largest-selling line in the whole category here, and a ~70%-share brand means Parachute is a price-compared traffic item at thin margin. COLD-HILL TRAP: coconut oil solidifies below roughly 24°C, so from November to March every narrow-neck bottle on this shelf is a solid block a customer cannot pour. Stock wide-mouth jars and squeeze packs for winter, and expect complaints if you only carry the tall bottle. Also watch cost — the 2025 copra price surge pushed coconut-oil MRPs up sharply, so re-check landed cost before repeating a purchase price.

skuLines.line: Coconut oil — large jar / tin / family pack
skuLines.examples: Parachute 1L jar, Nihar 1L, Shalimar tin, local 5L tin
skuLines.notes: A married-quarters family oiling four heads of uncut hair buys litres, not millilitres. Wide-mouth jar is essential in winter for the solidification reason above. Best rupees-per-kg of freight in the whole category — the right thing to fill a hill truck with.

skuLines.examples: Parachute sachet, Nihar pouch, Shalimar pouch
skuLines.notes: The pocket-money pack, and the one that gains share whenever coconut prices rise — down-packing is how rural India absorbs oil inflation. A pouch also solves the winter solidification problem better than a bottle does.

skuLines.examples: Parachute Advansed Aloe Vera, Parachute Advansed Jasmine, Nihar Shanti Amla, Parachute Ayurvedic
skuLines.notes: Meaningfully better margin than plain Parachute for the same shelf space, and the fragrance genuinely matters when oiled hair sits under a turban or patka all day. Trade customers up from plain coconut here.

skuLines.examples: Dabur Amla, Dabur Amla Gold, Kesh Nikhar, Bajaj Amla
skuLines.notes: The canonical long-hair oil of North India and directly on-point for a population growing hair for life — amla is the ingredient the tradition itself names. Expect this to index far above a normal store.

skuLines.examples: Bajaj Almond Drops, Hair & Care, Keo Karpin, Emami 7 Oils in One
skuLines.notes: The 'oil I can wear to class' segment — young people reject heavy coconut for daytime and this is the compromise that keeps the oiling habit alive. Also the oil that does not solidify in a cold room, which is a quiet competitive advantage here from November.

skuLines.examples: Local kachi ghani, Dhara, Patanjali, Fortune
skuLines.notes: Punjabi and Himachali households genuinely oil hair and scalp with mustard, especially for children and in cold weather. Distinguish clearly from edible mustard oil on the shelf even though households cross-use it. Rancidity is the real risk — mustard turns faster than coconut, so date-rotate and avoid deep stock.

skuLines.line: Ayurvedic medicated hair oil — hairfall and greying
skuLines.examples: Indulekha Bringha, Kesh King, Sesa, Mahabhringraj, Dabur Vatika Enriched
skuLines.notes: High-value, high-margin, and it fits both the Ayurvedic lean of the institution and the intense concern about hair loss where hair is uncut by faith. Kesh King alone is a ~₹991 Cr brand at ~27% share of its segment, and Dabur bought 51% of Sesa Care in Nov-2024 — this is a segment with real marketing push behind it. Carry 4-5 SKUs across ₹150 to ₹500.

skuLines.examples: Navratna, Himgange, Himtaj, Nihar Naturals cooling
skuLines.seasonality: Short summer only (May-Jun); genuinely dead Nov-Mar
skuLines.notes: Honest correction to the national pattern: Navratna is a ~66%-share, ₹1,026 Cr brand and would be a must-have in the plains, but a cold hill township at 173101 suppresses cooling-oil demand for most of the year. Stock it — headache and stress relief sells year-round to staff — but keep depth LOW and do not let a distributor push a plains-sized order onto you.

skuLines.line: Modern claim hair oil — onion / rosemary / multi-oil
skuLines.examples: Mamaearth Onion Hair Oil, WOW Onion, Wishcare, Pilgrim Redensyl
skuLines.notes: Where the 18-25 cohort's oil money goes. Rosemary is the ingredient currently taking over from onion at the premium end. Good margin; keep it to 3-4 SKUs so it does not cannibalise the Ayurvedic shelf.

skuLines.examples: Johnson's Baby Oil, Dabur Lal Tail, Himalaya Baby Oil, Mamaearth
skuLines.notes: Daily infant oil massage is near-universal in Indian households and intensifies in a cold hill winter. Dabur Lal Tail in particular has no substitute in the mother's mind — a stockout is not forgiven. Non-negotiable for the married-staff quarters.

skuLines.examples: Castor oil, sesame (til) oil, olive oil, argan, Bajaj Castor, Patanjali
skuLines.notes: Castor is the volume seller of this group (brows, lashes, hair-growth home remedies). Olive is on-brand for a Jivo unit and worth a facing. Keep this a 3-4 SKU curiosity shelf, not a range.

skuLines.line: Loose / refillable hair oil from bulk tin
skuLines.examples: Local coconut, mustard, amla oil dispensed from 5-15L tins
skuLines.notes: Highest-margin oil option and the cheapest per ml for a large family — a strong combination in a captive market. Needs a Legal Metrology-compliant weighing/measuring setup and clean dispensing; keep the source tin's batch and expiry on display. Also the single best answer to hill freight: you ship oil, not bottles and air.

skuLines.examples: Godrej Nupur, Khadi Natural, Banjara's, local loose henna
skuLines.notes: The culturally safest grey-coverage option in a Sikh institution — a plant dye and a conditioning pack rather than a chemical alteration, so it sells where a tube of black dye will not. Colour lands orange-to-auburn on its own and goes brown-to-black only when mixed with indigo, so stock both and say so at the counter. Powder cakes and loses potency in a heavy monsoon — 12-18 month practical life, sealed storage, avoid over-ordering before the rains.

skuLines.line: Indigo powder / natural black hair dye
skuLines.examples: Khadi Indigo, Banjara's Neel, Godrej Nupur with indigo, local neel
skuLines.notes: Sold only in company with henna — indigo is what turns henna's orange into brown or black. Attach-sell the pair with a written mixing ratio; the commonest complaint in this line is a customer who used indigo alone and got a blue-green result.

skuLines.line: Herbal hair pack / amla-brahmi-shikakai colouring pack
skuLines.examples: Indus Valley, Khadi, Patanjali Kesh Kanti hair pack, local mixes
skuLines.notes: Sits between henna and treatment. Sells on the same natural-and-Ayurvedic instinct that drives the herbal shampoo shelf; good margin, no cold-chain, long life if kept dry.

skuLines.line: Creme hair colour kit — black/brown, unisex
skuLines.examples: Godrej Expert Rich Creme, Garnier Color Naturals, L'Oreal Casting Creme Gloss, Streax
skuLines.notes: Read the room on depth. Many observant Sikhs do not dye hair or beard at all, so this shelf serves non-Sikh staff, some older residents and wedding occasions — real demand, but a fraction of what the same population size would buy elsewhere. The ₹35-40 single-use sachet kit is the right lead SKU here, not the ₹350 box. Statutory PPD/ammonia patch-test warning must be on pack; 24-36 month shelf life.

skuLines.examples: Godrej Powder Hair Dye, Super Vasmol 33, Black Rose
skuLines.notes: The cheapest grey coverage in India and the mainstay for older male staff and support workers — Godrej, Black Rose and Super Vasmol are the three that compete for this shelf. Keep it discreetly placed given the setting. Shallow depth, high rotation.

skuLines.line: Beard oil / beard wash / beard serum
skuLines.examples: Beardo, Bombay Shaving Company, Ustraa, Man Arden
skuLines.notes: The most under-stocked line for a Sikh male population and one of the best-margin ones. Uncut beards need washing, conditioning, softening and combing exactly as scalp hair does, and in dry cold they itch. A beard comb, beard oil and a beard wash is a three-SKU bundle with almost no competition within 30km.

skuLines.line: Root touch-up stick / grey-coverage spray or comb
skuLines.examples: Streax Root Touch-Up, Godrej Expert Easy 5, BBLUNT, L'Oreal Magic Retouch
skuLines.notes: An occasion purchase before a function or a photograph. One or two facings. Aerosol versions carry the same flammability and transport caveat as hairspray.

skuLines.examples: Brylcreem, Parachute Advansed hair cream, Nivea Men, Set Wet cream
skuLines.notes: More relevant here than gel or wax — a cream tames and conditions rather than sculpting a cut, which is what a man with long tied hair or a beard actually wants. The winter dryness angle sells it.

skuLines.examples: Set Wet, Gatsby, Beardo, Ustraa
skuLines.notes: Deliberately shallow. Styling product assumes a cut hairstyle, which most of this male population does not have — this shelf serves non-Sikh students and staff only. Two or three SKUs; resist any distributor scheme that sizes this like a normal town.

skuLines.examples: Streax Hold & Play, Schwarzkopf Taft, BBLUNT Spa, Livon heat protect
skuLines.notes: Buys for functions and for girls using straighteners in hostel. Aerosols are flammable and pressurised — store away from heaters, check the transporter accepts them on the hill route, and check expiry on slow-moving cans.

skuLines.examples: Neem-wood kangha, sheesham kangha, plastic kangha, small under-turban size
skuLines.packSizes: Small (under-turban) / medium / large; wood and plastic
skuLines.notes: This is not an accessory here, it is an article of faith — one of the Five Ks, mandated in 1699, carried in the hair under the turban and used twice a day. It is lost, snapped and replaced constantly across 5,000 people. Highest margin in the entire category, no expiry, tiny freight cube, and zero risk of being undercut. If any line in hair care deserves real depth and multiple sizes, it is this one.

skuLines.examples: Roots, Vega, Ghadi, generic dressing comb, tail comb, wide-tooth
skuLines.notes: Wide-tooth is the workhorse for waist-length wet hair; a fine dressing comb will tear it. Stock wide-tooth deeper than the standard comb, which is the reverse of a normal store's mix. No expiry, high margin, negligible freight.

skuLines.examples: Mediker nit comb, Vega lice comb, generic double-sided steel comb
skuLines.seasonality: With every dorm lice outbreak; term-start peak
skuLines.notes: Manual nit removal is a documented core part of treatment, not an optional extra, so this sells one-per-treatment and often one-per-child. Cheap, high margin, never expires. Always bundled with the anti-lice shampoo — never let one be in stock without the other.

skuLines.examples: Vega, Roots, Filone, generic paddle brush
skuLines.notes: Durable, no expiry, good margin. A soft baby brush-and-comb set is a separate must-stock for the married quarters.

skuLines.line: Hair ties, elastics, rubber bands, jooda and U-pins
skuLines.examples: Generic black elastics, jooda pins, U-pins, bobby pins, hair nets, dasturband ties
skuLines.notes: The quiet winner of this category at this site. Five thousand people with uncut hair tie it up every single day, pins and elastics are lost or snapped constantly, and there is no alternative supplier within 30km. Cheapest freight cube, best margin, no expiry, no obsolescence. Stock black as the default — school uniform rules almost always specify it.

skuLines.examples: Generic claw clips, snap clips, school ribbons, cloth hairbands
skuLines.notes: Keep the school-compliant colours (black, white, navy) as the core and treat fashion colours as a small seasonal add. Modest-dress norms mean plain and traditional outsells novelty here.

skuLines.line: Hair-care sundries — oiling applicator, scalp massager, shower cap, hair towel
skuLines.examples: Oil applicator comb bottle, wooden or silicone scalp massager, shower cap, microfibre hair wrap
skuLines.notes: Cheap, high-margin impulse items that pair naturally with the oil shelf. A microfibre hair wrap is a genuinely good sell in a cold climate where drying very long hair is a daily problem.

skuLines.examples: Philips, Havells, Vega, Syska, Nova
skuLines.notes: Low margin, high ticket, and it plugs a real off-campus leak — a dryer is exactly what someone buys on a town trip along with a month of other shopping. Constraints to be honest about: warranty service is 30-50km away so keep boxes and bills, check hostel electrical rules before pushing dryers to students, and hold 2-3 SKUs only. A dryer also has a straightforward winter story for drying long hair.

trends2026: Scalp-first care — the 'skinification' of the scalp. Scalp serums, pre-wash scalp treatments, scalp scrubs and exfoliants have moved from D2C into mass, and the claim has shifted from hair strand to follicle and scalp barrier. For a cold, dry, turban-wearing population this is the most genuinely relevant new segment on the list.

Coconut-oil input cost inflation reshaping the oil shelf. The 2025 copra price surge pushed Parachute/Nihar-tier MRPs up sharply, which drives down-packing (shoppers move to sachets and smaller bottles rather than dropping the habit) and pulls volume toward light almond and non-coconut oils. Re-check landed cost every purchase cycle rather than repeating last year's price.

The hairfall-actives ladder has moved on from onion. Onion (Mamaearth, WOW) is now mainstream shelf furniture; the premium end has shifted to rosemary oil, redensyl, capixyl and peptide blends sold by 'clinical' D2C brands (Minimalist, Foxtale, Deconstruct, Pilgrim) with percentages printed on the label. Percentage-on-pack is the new premium signal.

Sachets and low-unit packs are not dying. Ten-minute delivery has not displaced the ₹1-4 sachet in small-town and institutional India — inflation has reinforced it as the entry point. For a captive campus with pocket-money buyers, the sachet strip remains a core fixture, not a legacy one.

'Ayurveda with proof' consolidating under big FMCG. Indulekha, Kesh King, Sesa (Dabur took 51% of Sesa Care in Nov-2024) and Patanjali are pushing heritage ingredients — bhringraj, amla, reetha, shikakai, onion — with modern claim substantiation and real media spend behind them. This is where margin and credibility now overlap.

Clean-label claims moving down-price. Sulphate-free, silicone-free and paraben-free have crossed from ₹600 premium into the ₹200-350 mass-premium band, and refill pouches, concentrates and shampoo bars are appearing on sustainability grounds — which also happens to cut freight weight, a real advantage on a hill route.

Men's hair and beard care as a distinct segment rather than a styling afterthought. Beard oil, beard wash and beard serum plus men's anti-hairfall regimens (Beardo, Bombay Shaving Company, Ustraa, and telehealth players like Traya and Man Matters) have built national awareness that now shows up as in-store demand — particularly relevant where beards are uncut by faith.

Q-commerce has made serums, masks and dry shampoo impulse buys in metros — which inverts here. No 10-minute channel reaches Baru Sahib, so the store itself has to hold the impulse depth that a Blinkit basket would otherwise absorb. Anything a resident sees advertised and cannot buy on campus becomes a reason to shop in town.
adjacentServices: Term-start hair kit sold at admission and dorm check-in — kangha, spare elastics and jooda pins, wide-tooth comb, steel nit comb, hair oil and shampoo in one pre-priced bundle. Highest-margin mix in the category, perfectly predictable timing, and it captures the spend before a family's town trip does.

Scheduled lice screening and dormitory treatment drives with the Academy health room, once or twice a term. An outbreak needs a whole dorm treated in the same week — running it as a planned service with a pre-built shampoo-plus-nit-comb kit turns a stockout emergency into forecastable revenue.

Hair oil refill station — dispense coconut, mustard and amla oil from 5-15L tins into the customer's own bottle. Cuts the customer's price per ml, lifts gross margin to 30-50%, and cuts hill freight substantially because you ship oil instead of bottles and air. Needs a Legal Metrology-compliant measure and visible batch/expiry from the source tin.

Standing institutional indent to hostels, wardens and the junior school for bulk shampoo, oil and combs. Low margin, zero impulse risk, and it moves volume through the warehouse rather than the POS counter.

Winter scalp bundle, pushed Nov-Feb — hair oil plus anti-dandruff shampoo plus a mask or leave-in, at a set price. Dandruff is documented to worsen in the cold and this is the one demand spike at this site you can predict months ahead.

Ladies' hair-wash, champi and hair-spa service, plus a men's grooming and beard-trim counter for non-observant staff and students. Attaches directly to the retail shelf and keeps service spend on campus — but scope it carefully with the Trust, since hair-cutting services are culturally sensitive in this setting.

WhatsApp reorder and quarters delivery for married staff families — the cohort with babies, the least free time and the most to lose from a stockout. No q-commerce competes for this, so a simple reorder list captures the repeat purchase that would otherwise wait for a town trip.

CONSEQUENCE for how to read this list: the SKU-line structure, cohort mapping, essentiality calls, seasonality and the hill/Sikh-institution reasoning are the parts I stand behind. The specific brand examples, pack sizes, price bands and margin bands are my own Indian-retail trade knowledge as of the 2025-26 season, NOT figures verified against a live page in this session — treat them as planning estimates to be checked against a current distributor price list before any buying decision. Confidence: high on structure and cohort fit, moderate on price bands (±20%), moderate on margin bands.

VERIFIED IN SESSION — Wikipedia, Kesh (Sikhism): uncut hair as one of the Five Ks; hair combed twice daily with a kangha, tied in a joora/rishi knot, held by the kangha and covered by turban, patka or rumal. This is the single most load-bearing fact in the list.

VERIFIED IN SESSION — Wikipedia, Kangha (Sikhism): small wooden comb, one of the Five Ks, mandated 1699, used twice a day, kept in the hair beneath the turban behind the rishi knot. Basis for treating the kangha as a must-have with real depth.

VERIFIED IN SESSION — Wikipedia, Dandruff: caused by sebum, Malassezia globosa and individual susceptibility; actives are ketoconazole, zinc pyrithione, selenium disulfide, coal tar, salicylic acid; 'the condition may worsen in the winter'. Basis for the Nov-Feb anti-dandruff spike at a cold hill site.

VERIFIED IN SESSION — Wikipedia, Head louse: head-to-head contact is by far the dominant transmission route; ages 4-14 have the highest infestation rates; girls infested two to four times more often than boys; nitpicking with combs is a core treatment alongside pediculicides. Basis for anti-lice shampoo plus nit comb as the highest-regret must-have in a residential school.

VERIFIED IN SESSION — Wikipedia, Henna: hair colour lands orange to auburn to burgundy depending on base hair and henna quality; mixing with indigo achieves brown and black shades; sold as powder. Basis for stocking henna and indigo as an attach-sold pair.

VERIFIED IN SESSION — Wikipedia, Hair conditioner: rinse-out/instant, deep conditioner/hair mask (20-30 min), leave-in (silicones and film-forming polymers), 2-in-1 conditioning shampoo, cleansing conditioner/co-wash. Basis for the conditioner and treatment sub-structure.

VERIFIED IN SESSION — Wikipedia, Hair care: product taxonomy across colouring, conditioner, gel, mousse, serum, spray, tonic, wax, pomade, and the cleansing/conditioning/styling/colour/scalp functional split.

VERIFIED IN SESSION — Wikipedia, Shampoo: the word derives from Hindi cā̃pō and originally meant an Indian head massage with hair oils; early effective shampoo was sapindus (soapberry) boiled with dried amla and herbs; shikakai, hibiscus, ritha and arappu in historical use.
